title: Wilhelm von Fürstenberg, Vienna, to Jobst Edmund von Brabeck, dean of Münster, 10 July 1659 (catalogue 1645): the five cipher runs read; the filed number key belongs to another system, the letter cipher is a two-alphabet shift (Vigenère 'bi' on 24 letters) found ciphertext-only

steps.what: Images 84-87 fetched from the LAV NRW image server, one at a time, 2 s apart.
Sign conventions written before any key; the 15 cipher lines transcribed by shape in two passes (2x and 3x crops) and reconciled on the image.
Filed number key tested: the letter has no numbers; a letter-to-digit search over letter pairs against the table's numbers gave no German.

Index of coincidence 0.052 overall, 0.065 and 0.080 for odd and even places of each run; a Caesar fit per set against German/Latin letter frequencies gave shifts 1 and 8 on the 24-letter alphabet. Key frozen (key_frozen.tsv).

Shifts refitted blind on runs P1-P3 only and applied to P4-P5: 159/159 letters (100%) agree with the reading. Reverse fold (fit P4-P5, test P1-P3): same shifts, 185/186 (99.5%), the miss being the encipherer's slip in quob. The key was first found on all five runs, so this is a re-fit test.

Runs decrypted mechanically and read as German-Latin clauses with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds the decryption and fails on any unmarked departure (passes). 53 of 54 words verbatim, 1 marked repair, no holes.
Two web searches on Fürstenberg, Brabeck, 1659 and on Hüttenhain's book: no edition or decipherment of this letter found; Hüttenhain 1974 not seen.

Independent blind review by an AI language-model agent that took no part in the solution: six cipher lines transcribed from the images before the solver's transcription was opened (201 of 202 signs agree; the one difference is the fourth sign of 85.4, e or c, now written c? and marked in the reading); check_marks and the held-out test re-run; the five runs read as sentences against the translation (5 of 5 clean, no holes). The P1 translation now brackets the supplied words.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 345 tokens, 41 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.349 per letter; random keys -6.685 (z 10.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.613 (mean -3.694, z 20.5); annealer on the real text -3.105. Verdict: pass.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026), second AI language-model reader: decryption re-made with an own decoder from the stated shifts (identical on all five runs); German model de-1640s per letter: the true shifts (1, 8) -3.90, the best of the other 575 shift pairs -7.62, their mean -9.53; 500 random substitution-alphabet pairs max -7.87; 300 within-run shuffles of the ciphertext under the true key max -8.09. The shifts are not an overfit of a two-parameter key to 345 letters.

Integration check: image 085 fetched from the Landesarchiv NRW; the ten cipher lines of page 1 read against the transcription at reduced size (all agree), and full-resolution crops of 85.4 (fourth sign an open c with a small tick, as c?) and of 85.9-85.10 agree. Image 086 not compared. Strict read share recomputed: 52 of 54 words (96.3%), the word on the uncertain sign not counted as verbatim.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.314; polyphony 0.003; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.105

outcome.method_basis: Ciphertext-only: period found from the index of coincidence of alternate places, the two shifts from letter frequencies; tested by refitting on part of the text and reading the rest.
outcome.fraction_read_source: All five cipher runs of the letter (345 letters, 54 words); strict count: 52 words verbatim from the signs, one (wort) on an uncertain sign (counted as not read) and one with a marked repaired letter (quo{b/d}); the contributor's own count, with wort as verbatim, is 53 of 54 (98.1%).

texts.label: Letter of 10 July 1659, Vienna: five cipher runs
texts.summary: News from the imperial court: the president of the Aulic Council, Count Oettingen, and Prince Auersperg say the court will keep the word the Emperor gave in writing from Frankfurt and the Prince (the Prince-Bishop of Münster) will have the judgement for himself without any condition of Doctor Batz; 700 Reichstaler promised to the referent von Lindenspür are to be transferred; postscript: everything was concluded today in the secret council in the Prince's favour with no condition attached.
texts.note: Five runs, each a clause or sentence in mixed German and Latin set into a German letter. 54 words: strict count (README read bar) 52 verbatim from the signs (96.3%); the contributor's own count is 53 (98.1%), which includes wor{t?}, a word on an uncertain sign (85.4, written c?; as e it would be the repair wor{w/t}), and is theirs; 1 with a marked repair (quo{b/d}, an open c where e is needed, most likely the encipherer's slip); 0 holes. Dan's checker gives 0.40 on the five runs alone (2 of 5 sentences clean): it judges each sentence in one language, and its unknown words are the mixed-language words, names (Ottingen, Aursbergius, Batz, Lindenspur) and period spellings (konditione, reichsdalers, uberwexelen, concludiret, siebenhundert). Read by hand, 5 of 5 runs are clean with no holes. Whole reading file 0.48; translation 0.727. Outside the cipher and left open (NOTES.md, Remaining gaps): the clear German text of the letter was not transcribed ('doctoris Batz' not identified), and the number key on image 86, which belongs to another cipher, was not traced.

reading_review.note: Read all five runs as German-Latin sentences against the translation: 5 of 5 clean, no holes, one marked repair (quod); a blind sign spot-check of six lines gave 201 of 202 signs, the one difference being the flagged 85.4 sign (e or c), which changes at most one letter of 'wort'. Dan's checker gives 0.40 on the runs because of mixed German and Latin, names and period spellings, not holes.

gaps.detail: Not online; may print this letter or describe this cipher. Interlibrary loan needed.

Ambiguous on the scan: e at 2x, a ticked c at 4x; the original or a better image would settle it. As c it gives 'wort'; as e 'worw', a repair wor{w/t} (52 of 54 verbatim, 96.3%). The blind reviewer confirmed c for 85.2 and for the slip in 85.7.

prior.where: No edition or decipherment found in two web searches (12 Nov 2026) or in the vetting of 4 Nov 2026 (DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry). Hüttenhain, Die Geheimschriften des Fürstbistums Münster unter Christoph Bernhard von Galen 1650-1678 (Münster 1974) not seen; it may describe this system or print the letter.

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1645) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, found and tested the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
